english.title: Import a class B drug with intent to evade a prohibition / restriction
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), with intent to evade any prohibition or restriction for the time being in force with respect to drugs by or under any enactment,

(A)_[unloaded from a ship, namely **(..SPECIFY..),]_
(B)_[landed in a port, namely **(..SPECIFY..),]_
(C)_[unloaded from an aircraft, namely **(..SPECIFY..),]_

a class B drug, namely **(..SPECIFY THE CLASS 'B' DRUG AND QUANTITY..)
english.legislation: Contrary to section 50(2)(a), (4) and (5) of and Schedule 1 to the Customs and Excise Management Act 1979.

investigatoraction.description: Criminal lifestyle offence under Schedule 2 to POCA - consider confiscation order

DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) See section 171 for general provisions as to offences and penalties.
(ii) This offence specifically caters for importation whereby the appropriate duty is evaded.
(iii) For the import/export of a class 'B' drug in breach of a restriction/prohibition on that importation/exporting by virtue of section 3 of the Misuse of Drugs Act 1971 see H3622 and H3623.
(iv) See section 49 for forfeiture provisions

other.penalty:
SUMMARY: Six months imprisonment and / or a fine of £20,000 or of three times the value of the goods, whichever is the greater.
INDICTMENT: Fourteen years imprisonment and / or a fine.
